ACC Tournament champions |bowl = [[2011 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] |bowl_result = Sweet Sixteen }} {{2010–11 ACC men's basketball standings}} The '''2010–11 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team''' represented [[Duke University]] in the [[2010–11 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. Returning as head coach was [[Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame|Hall of Famer]] [[Mike Krzyzewski]]. The team played its home games at [[Cameron Indoor Stadium]] in [[Durham, North Carolina]] and are members of the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]]. The team finished the regular season with a record of 30–4, ranked #1 in the media polls a total of eleven weeks during the season. They also won the [[2011 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]], winning for the third consecutive year. As the #1 seed in the west region of the [[2011 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament]], they defeated [[Hampton University|Hampton]] in the second round and [[2010–11 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|Michigan]] in the third round to advance to the ''Sweet Sixteen'' where they were defeated by [[2010–11 Arizona Wildcats men's basketball team|Arizona]] to finish the season 32–5. ==Previous season== The team finished [[2009–10 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|2010]] with a 35–5 record, becoming the ACC Regular Season Co-Champion, ACC tournament champion, and earning a #1 seed in the [[2010 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament]]. The Blue Devils beat [[2009–10 Butler Bulldogs men's basketball team|Butler]] in the championship game 61–59 to win the fourth national championship in school history. ==Pre-season== ===Recruiting=== Duke came out and took care of business with a commanding 39–22 lead going into halftime. As the game continued, Duke built a larger margin and easily took the first game of the tournament, beating Hampton 87–45. After Kyrie Irving suffered a toe injury in December and missed 26 games, he made his return against Hampton. After a slow start, Irving led the team in scoring with 14 points while playing 20 minutes. {{Clear}} ===Third round: Michigan=== {| class="wikitable" align=right |- bgcolor=#ffdead align=center | colspan=1 | '''Teams''' | colspan=1 | '''1st''' | colspan=1 | '''2nd''' | colspan=1 | '''Final''' |- | '''(8) MICH''' | align=center | 33 | align=center | 38 | align=center | '''71''' |- | '''(1) DUKE''' | align=center | 37 | align=center | 36 | align=center | '''73''' |- |} Duke continued their 2011 NCAA Tournament bid with a third-round match up with the [[2010-11 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|Michigan Wolverines]]. Duke opened the game going back and forth with Michigan, going into halftime with a 38–33 lead. However, even after leading by 15 points midway through the second half, the Wolverines would not go away. Bringing the game down to the final seconds, it was Duke who prevailed behind [[Nolan Smith|Nolan Smith's]] 24 and beat Michigan 73–71 moving them on to the Sweet Sixteen in [[Anaheim, California|Anaheim]]. This victory also gave coach [[Mike Krzyzewski]] his 900th career victory, becoming only the fourth coach to accomplish this feat. {{Clear}} ===Regional semifinal: Arizona=== {| class="wikitable" align=right |- bgcolor=#ffdead align=center | colspan=1 | '''Teams''' | colspan=1 | '''1st''' | colspan=1 | '''2nd''' | colspan=1 | '''Final''' |- | '''(5) ARIZ''' | align=center | 38 | align=center | 55 | align=center | '''93''' |- | '''(1) DUKE''' | align=center | 44 | align=center | 33 | align=center | '''77''' |- |} Duke played well in the first half and was up by 6 points at halftime. Arizona was only kept within range by a stellar performance by Wildcats forward [[Derrick Williams (basketball)|Derrick Williams]], who scored 25 of his 32 points in the first half.
